{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sc-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3e148b43f2ba77e7878674dfc0d11e2ae89e09bdc4566e45d2fc89187b142992","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sc-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"61c32f86a25e3c021742b3c9ddf64a97709817dd75a19df6d2b69eac0a40c4f1","source_liveness_sha256":"feb7871590284d2a19ab0509ff65b48154ba15e637a6ec9b839f55a72736ffdb"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"License classes, beginner's permit, graduated license and required tests","heading":"C — License classes, documents, the beginner's permit, graduated driver's license stages and the required tests","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — License classes, documents, the beginner's permit, graduated driver's license stages and the required tests
Knowledge domain: which South Carolina license class fits which vehicle, what a first-time applicant must bring, how the beginner's permit and the graduated license stages work for teens, and what the vision, knowledge and skills tests demand.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
A Class D license covers non-commercial passenger vehicles, such as cars and trucks, that weigh no more than 26,000 pounds GVW. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A02
Class E and Class F holders, like Class D holders, may also operate a moped or a three-wheel vehicle, but not a two-wheel motorcycle with a detachable sidecar. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A02
Class E covers non-commercial single-unit vehicles above 26,000 pounds GVW, such as big trucks and motor homes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A02
Class F covers non-commercial combination vehicles above 26,000 pounds GVW, such as a truck or motor home pulling a trailer or another vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A02
Class G is the moped license: the minimum age is 15 and only the vision and knowledge tests are required. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A02
A driver who already holds a valid license or permit in any of the other four classes needs no separate license to ride a moped. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A02
Class M covers two-wheel motorcycles, with or without a detachable sidecar, and three-wheel vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A03
A Class A CDL covers vehicle combinations with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more when the towed unit's GVWR is over 10,000 pounds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A03
A Class B CDL covers a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, including one towing no more than 10,000 pounds GVWR. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A03
A Class C CDL covers vehicles that fit neither Class A nor B but are designed to carry 16 or more people counting the driver, or are placarded for hazardous materials. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A03
Each qualified driver holds just one license endorsed for one or more classes, and having more than one valid license is illegal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A03
Behind the wheel you must have a valid license, the vehicle registration and a valid insurance card for that class of vehicle, or you can be fined. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A04
A US citizen applying for a first permit, license or ID card brings originals that prove US citizenship, identity, birth date and birthplace, Social Security number and South Carolina address, as listed on form MV-93. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A04
An applicant who is not a US citizen applies at a branch that processes international customers, following the checklist on form MV-94. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A04
Anyone who has never held a driver's license starts with a beginner's permit, which requires an age of at least 15 and passing the vision and knowledge tests. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A04
On a beginner's permit you may drive from 6 a.m. to midnight with a licensed driver in the front seat who is at least 21 and has at least one year of experience. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A04
Permit driving after midnight needs supervision by a licensed person from the list in SC Code §56-1-100(A)(1-7). [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A05
The earliest you may apply for any license after getting a beginner's permit is the 181st day, and any day after that also works. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A05
A permit holder who is 15 or 16 must practice at least 40 hours, with ten of those hours at night, beside an approved supervisor such as a father, mother or legal guardian. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A05
A first-time applicant aged 17 or older must have held a beginner's permit for more than 180 days before taking the skills test for full privileges. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A06
A first-time applicant aged 15 or 16 must have completed driver's education with eight hours in the classroom and six hours of driving. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A06
That teen applicant must also be enrolled in school, not suspended or expelled, and have satisfactory attendance. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A07
Teens submit form PDLA, the Certification of School Attendance, Driver's Education and Driving Practice, which the driver's education program hands out after the course is passed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A07
The graduated driver's license program serves ages 15 to 17 and limits night and unsupervised driving at first, easing those limits over time. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A07
A conditional license is open to applicants at least 15 and a half but under 16 who pass the vision and skills tests. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A07
A conditional licensee may drive alone from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., or until 8 p.m. during daylight saving time, and with a licensed driver aged 21 or older from then until midnight. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A07
Conditional and special restricted licensees may carry at most two passengers under 21 unless a licensed adult aged 21 or older rides along, except when carrying family members or students to and from school. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A07
A conditional licensee earns full privileges after holding the license for one year with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collisions. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A08
From midnight to 6 a.m., conditional and special restricted licensees may drive only when supervised by a licensed person from the list in SC Code §56-1-100(A)(1-7). [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A08
A driver under 17 who collects six or more points before holding the license for one year has it suspended for six months. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A08
The special restricted license is for applicants who are 16 but under 17 and pass the vision and skills tests, or who are 16 and already hold a conditional license. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A09
A 16-year-old with a special restricted or conditional license may get a waiver to drive alone until midnight for work or certain extracurricular activities, but never after midnight. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A09
The waiver needs a branch visit with form 447-NC, the Consent for Minor form 447-CM signed by a qualified adult before SCDMV staff, two letters, a vision test and a $25 fee. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A09
Full privileges arrive at 17, or after a year on a conditional or special restricted license with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collisions, with no branch visit needed. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A10
Once you reach full privileges the SCDMV mails you a sleeve, and you must keep the license inside it to use those full privileges. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A10
An original license or an upgrade to a different class requires vision, knowledge and skills tests, and the vision and knowledge tests can be taken at any SCDMV branch. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A10
You fail the knowledge test if you leave the test area before finishing, talk to anyone, or bring in written material or any electronic device such as a phone, laptop or tablet. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A10
One Stop Driver Training and Testing Programs, also called third-party testers, may give the knowledge and/or skills tests for a first-time Class D permit or license and a Class M license. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A11
The SCDMV may randomly select an applicant to pass the skills test again before the license is issued, under SC Code §56-1-15. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A11
Every first license test includes vision, knowledge and skills tests except the moped license, which needs no skills test. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A11
You must provide the skills test vehicle, and it must be safe with working headlights, brakes, windshield wipers, mirrors and speedometer. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A12
The test vehicle also needs working safety belts, turn signals, defroster and horn, plus a valid license plate, registration card and insurance card. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F43 | anchor: A12
An unsafe vehicle gets the skills test postponed, and not wearing your seat belt during the test is an automatic fail. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F44 | anchor: A12
Bring your old license or permit if you have one, a licensed driver, and liability insurance information from a company licensed to do business in SC. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F45 | anchor: A12
Only you and the SCDMV employee who tests you may be in or around the vehicle. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F46 | anchor: A12
The knowledge test covers traffic laws, road signs and driving safety rules, and corrective lenses should be brought or worn for the vision test. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F47 | anchor: A12
Skills test tasks may include working the lights, wipers, signals and four-way flashers, a brake light check, lane changes and turns, naming signs, parallel parking, 100 feet of straight backing, hill parking and a reverse two-point turnabout. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0017]

Misconceptions: a Class D license covers mopeds and three-wheel vehicles but never a motorcycle with a sidecar; the permit holding period applies at every age, not only to teens; the waiver extends solo driving to midnight but never past it; an unbuckled seat belt fails the skills test outright; full privileges arrive automatically without a branch visit.
Mnemonics: forty and ten for teen practice, forty hours total with ten after dark; for the permit, hold it one hundred eighty days and apply from day one hundred eighty-one; the curfew ladder is alone until six in the evening (eight in daylight saving time), an adult of twenty-one until midnight, a listed supervisor after that.
Glossary: GVWR means the gross vehicle weight rating set for a vehicle; beginner's permit means the learner permit every never-licensed driver starts with; conditional license means the first teen stage from age fifteen and a half; special restricted license means the stage for sixteen-year-olds; PDLA means the school attendance, driver's education and practice certification; third-party tester means an SCDMV-authorized school that gives tests.
Dynamic facts: form numbers, the waiver fee, branch lists and the third-party tester list can change; confirm them on the SCDMV website before relying on them.
